candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is multifocal diverticulitis. The clinical record documents prior CT evidence of diverticulitis (paracolic haziness at descending-sigmoid junction), left-sided colitis on prior imaging, and now diffuse colonic wall thickening with pericolonic stranding — findings consistent with diverticular disease flaring at multiple sites. Ulcerative Colitis is a distinct inflammatory bowel disease with different pathophysiology, typical onset pattern, and endoscopic/histologic features. While UC can cause diffuse colitis, asserting UC as the diagnosis conflicts with the diverticulitis-centered reference diagnosis. The candidate is not merely a parent or component but an incompatible alternative etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Ulcerative Colitis (extensive) is an inflammatory bowel disease of different etiology and subtype than multifocal diverticulitis; both can cause diffuse colonic wall thickening but represent incompatible diagnostic entities

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis of 'multifocal diverticulitis' is plausible given prior imaging findings but colonoscopy was deferred, leaving histologic/endoscopic confirmation absent; PET-avid lesion raises unresolved malignancy concern that complicates diagnostic certainty
CEA of 1.7 is within normal range, somewhat arguing against colorectal malignancy but not definitive
